d: Ah! alas! Ay me! I fondly dream Had ye been there.' Milton.
Ay, adv. “Yes; yea; -- a word expressing assent, or an affirmative answer to a question. It is much used in viva voce voting in legislative bodies, etc.”
w.e: Perh. a modification of yea, or from the interjection of admiration or astonishment, OE. ei, ey, why, hey, ay, well, ah, ha. Cf. MHG. & G. ei, Dan. ej. Or perh. akin to aye ever.

d: A native nurse for children; also, a lady's maid. [India]
w.e: Pg. aia, akin to Sp. aya a governess, ayo a tutor.

n: (in India) a native nursemaid who looks after children

d: An affirmative vote; one who votes in the affirmative; as, To call for the ayes and noes; The ayes have it.
Ay, adv. “Always; ever; continually; for an indefinite time. For his mercies aye endure. Milton. For aye, always; forever; eternally.”
w.e: Icel. ei, ey; akin to AS. a, awa, always, Goth. aiws an age, Icel. æfi, OHG, , L. aevum, Gr. je, Skr. course. Age, v., Either, a., Or, conj.
From the native name, prob. from its cry.

n: nocturnal lemur with long bony fingers and rodent-like incisor teeth closely related to the lemurs
